key_insight: A local quadratic approximation can meaningfully predict LLM pretraining dynamics over surprisingly long training windows, making it a useful proxy for optimization behavior.
engineering_relevance: This suggests practitioners can analyze and potentially monitor large-scale training using tractable local curvature models, Hessian spectra, and stability diagnostics without fully simulating the full loss landscape.
method: Taylor-expand the model and loss around intermediate checkpoints to form local quadratic optimization problems.
Estimate deep Hessian spectral structure using Lanczos quadrature with very deep probes.
Evaluate local linear stability and compare it with theoretical edge-of-stability predictions across batch sizes and preconditioners.
evidence_signal: On a 150M-parameter model trained on 3B tokens, the quadratic model predicted optimization dynamics accurately over windows lasting up to 10% of training.
watch_item: The conclusions are local and checkpoint-dependent, so the proxy may break down outside the tested windows or when training setup, batch size, or preconditioner changes substantially.
paper_title: A Defense of the Quadratic Model
